newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wool market still finds buyers shy.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wool market still finds buyers shy.

text.p: Demand for finer merino wool at the first Australian sales on Wednesday pushed main market indicators to new seasonal peaks, but buyers further down the line weren't inspired and traders said they could not pass the higher prices on.

Activity, however, is not apparently depressed in most sectors, and combing in particular is much better placed than a few months ago - with tops for prompt delivery practically unobtainable, and delivery often now possible only four months ahead.
The fact that Wool International has been selling stockpile wool for delivery further forward tends to confirm these improvements.
But the May Day holiday kept Continental Europe out of the picture and the UK has its holiday on Monday.

The crossbred market recovered modestly in New Zealand after a disappointing Bradford auction of British wool. Activity is fair in the relevant sectors but world demand seems insufficient to push up prices at present.
